relations.evidence: In this example, the credentials (user="simon", pass="fizzbuzz") are given in the request header using basic authentication.

notable_absence.finding: The page authenticates as an ordinary named user ("simon") rather than as Administrator - the only page in this batch that does - yet says nothing about what privileges that user needs in order for the SELECT to succeed. Every other example on this API uses -u Administrator:password, which sidesteps the question entirely. So the batch demonstrates authentication without ever demonstrating authorization: no page states a required RBAC role or privilege. The requirement exists on the downstream reference page (server/current/n1ql-rest-query/index.md: "Users must have the relevant Administrative or Query & Index RBAC roles, depending on the types of query they intend to run") but is unreachable from here. privilege:query-select would be the object if this page stated it.

cross_component_finding: Note for reconciliation on the auth: namespace. This mechanism is HTTP Basic Authentication over the Query Service port, carried in the Authorization header. The corpus already contains sgw:basic-authentication (Sync Gateway) and sdk:authentication / sdk:certificate-authentication / sdk:ldap-authentication (SDK-side), plus security:authentication and capella:capella-ui-authentication. "Basic authentication" therefore now appears in at least three components with three different scopes. These should not be collapsed into one auth:basic-authentication: the Sync Gateway one authenticates to the Sync Gateway REST APIs, this one authenticates to the Query Service, and the underlying credential stores differ (Server RBAC users here, Sync Gateway users there). If reconciliation wants a shared parent, the right shape is a generic auth:http-basic-authentication with per-component subtypes, not a merge.
